newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices slip after retracing late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices slip after retracing late.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slipped late Monday, after partly retracing the day's earlier losses, in reaction to final U.N. clearance for Iraqi oil exports and expectations for milder weather in the U.S. Northeast.
January West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading at $25.10-20 a barrel, down 45 cents from late Friday's cash market.
Earlier in the afternoon, crude prices reached around 25.25-35 a barrel before slipping back.
The January/February WTI spread was around 47 cents, down three cts from earlier in the day and 13 cts from late Friday.
The grade differentials were subdued, with both sweets and sours weakening from Friday's levels.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James remained at 88-90 cents a barrel premium to WTI/Cushing, down three to five cents from late Friday.
West Texas Sour/Midland eased to a $1.90-95 discount to WTI/Cushing, down about five cents from Friday.
Sour grades, already plagued by oversupply, could drop further in reaction to Iraq's impending market re-entry, traders said.
